name: Aadhaar Card
description: A 12-digit unique identity number issued by UIDAI to all residents of India based on their biometric and demographic data.
authority: Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
eligibility: Any resident of India (who has resided in India for 182 days or more in the 12 months immediately preceding the date of application)
Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) holding a valid Indian Passport
No age limit (Baal Aadhaar issued for children below 5 years)
documents: Proof of Identity (POI) - e.g., Voter ID, Passport, PAN Card
Proof of Address (POA) - e.g., Bank Passbook, Utility Bill, Ration Card
Proof of Date of Birth (DOB) - e.g., Birth Certificate, SSLC Book

procedure: Locate an authorized Aadhaar Enrolment Centre online via uidai.gov.in or mAadhaar app
Book an appointment (optional but recommended)
Visit the centre with original supporting documents
Fill out the enrolment form and submit demographics
Provide biometric data (Iris scan, Fingerprints, and Photograph)
Collect the acknowledgment slip containing the Enrolment ID (EID) to track status

fees: Free for new enrolment. ₹50 for demographic/biometric update.
processingTime: Up to 30 days (usually generated within 7-15 days).

verification.notes: Verified against UIDAI enrolment guidelines.

name: Permanent Account Number (PAN) Card
description: A 10-character alphanumeric identifier issued by the Income Tax Department to track financial transactions and tax filings.
authority: Income Tax Department (Issued via NSDL/Protean and UTIITSL)
eligibility: Any Indian citizen, NRI, or foreign national engaging in financial transactions in India
Companies, firms, HUFs, and trusts
Minors can also hold a PAN card (applied through a guardian)
documents: Proof of Identity (Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport)
Proof of Address (Aadhaar, Utility bill, Passport)
Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate, Aadhaar, SSLC mark sheet)

procedure: Visit the NSDL (Protean) or UTIITSL PAN application portal
Select Form 49A (for Indian citizens/entities) or Form 49AA (for foreign entities)
Fill out the application with personal details and Aadhaar number
Complete e-KYC using Aadhaar OTP (for paperless mode) or upload scanned documents
Pay the application fee online
Digital e-PAN is sent via email, and the physical card is dispatched via post

fees: ₹107 (approx.) for physical PAN card dispatch within India; ₹72 for e-PAN only.
processingTime: e-PAN within 10 minutes to 48 hours; Physical card in 15-20 days.

verification.notes: Verified from Income Tax Department rules.

name: Voter ID Card (EPIC)
description: Electors Photo Identity Card (EPIC) issued by the Election Commission of India to eligible voters to exercise their democratic franchise.
authority: Election Commission of India (ECI)
eligibility: Must be an Indian citizen
Must be 18 years of age or older on the qualifying date (1st Jan, 1st April, 1st July, or 1st Oct)
Must be an ordinary resident of the polling area
documents: Recent passport size photograph
Proof of Age (Birth certificate, 10th mark sheet, PAN, Aadhaar)
Proof of Residence (Aadhaar, utility bill, rent agreement)

procedure: Visit the ECI Voters' Services Portal (voters.eci.gov.in) or use the Voter Helpline App
Register/Login and select 'Fill Form 6' (for new electoral roll registration)
Fill out personal, family, and address details
Upload photograph, age proof, and address proof
Submit the form and note the reference number
After verification by the Block Level Officer (BLO), EPIC is generated and delivered via post

fees: Free of cost.
processingTime: 1 to 2 months (depending on electoral roll revision cycles).

officialSources.sourceName: Election Commission of India - Voter Portal

verification.notes: Verified against ECI Form 6 guidelines.

name: Indian Passport
description: An official travel document issued by the Ministry of External Affairs certifying the identity and nationality of its holder for international travel.
authority: Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)
eligibility: Must be a citizen of India by birth, descent, registration, or naturalization
documents: Proof of Present Address (Aadhaar, Utility bill, Bank passbook)
Proof of Date of Birth (Birth certificate, 10th mark sheet, PAN)
Non-ECR Proof (10th/12th mark sheet, Degree certificate, if applicable)

procedure: Register on the Passport Seva portal (passportindia.gov.in)
Log in and select 'Apply for Fresh Passport/Re-issue of Passport'
Fill out the online application form and submit
Pay the exact fee online and book an appointment at the nearest Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or POPSK
Visit the PSK on the appointment date with original documents for verification, biometric capture, and photograph
Undergo police verification (pre or post issuance depending on applicant profile); passport is dispatched via Speed Post

fees: ₹1,500 for a standard 36-page passport (Normal). Additional fees apply for Tatkaal or 60-page booklets.
processingTime: Normal: 15-30 days (post-police verification). Tatkaal: 1-3 days.

verification.notes: Verified against MEA Passport Seva guidelines.

name: Driving License (DL)
description: An official document authorizing the holder to operate various types of motor vehicles on highways and public roads in India.
authority: State Regional Transport Offices (RTO) / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
eligibility: Must hold a valid Learner's License for the relevant vehicle class
Must apply for a permanent DL after 30 days and within 6 months of the Learner's License issue date
Minimum 18 years for LMV (Cars/Bikes with gear), 16 years for MCWOG (Bikes without gear, up to 50cc), 20 years for Transport Vehicles
documents: Valid Learner's License
Address Proof (Aadhaar, Passport, Voter ID)
Age Proof (Birth Certificate, PAN, 10th marksheet)
Passport size photographs

procedure: Visit the Sarathi Parivahan portal (parivahan.gov.in) and select your state
Click on 'Apply for Driving License'
Enter your Learner's License number and date of birth
Fill out the application, upload documents (if not fetched via Aadhaar), and pay the test and smart card fees
Book a driving test slot at your local RTO
Visit the RTO with your vehicle, pass the practical driving test, and the smart DL will be dispatched via post

fees: Varies by state (Typically ₹200 for DL grant + ₹200 for smart card + ₹300 for driving test).
processingTime: 7-15 days after passing the driving test.

verification.notes: Verified against MoRTH Sarathi portal.

name: Learner's License (LL)
description: A provisional license allowing an individual to practice driving on public roads under the supervision of a permanent driving license holder.
authority: State RTOs / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
eligibility: 16 years for motorcycles without gear (max 50cc, with parental consent)
18 years for Light Motor Vehicles (Cars and motorcycles with gear)
20 years for Commercial/Transport Vehicles
Must pass a computer-based traffic signs and rules test
documents: Age Proof
Address Proof
Medical Certificate Form 1A (if applying for transport vehicle or if age > 40)
Aadhaar Card (for contact-less e-KYC route)

procedure: Go to the Sarathi Parivahan portal and select 'Apply for Learner License'
Choose Aadhaar authentication (allows taking the test from home in most states) or non-Aadhaar (requires RTO visit)
Fill out the application, select vehicle classes, and upload documents/medical certificate
Pay the application and test fees
Watch the mandatory road safety tutorial video
Take the online LL computer test; upon passing, the LL can be downloaded immediately

fees: Varies by state (Typically ₹150 for LL grant + ₹50 for test).
processingTime: Instant generation upon passing the online test (for Aadhaar-based).

verification.notes: Verified against MoRTH online LL guidelines.

name: Unique Disability ID (UDID) Card
description: A single document of identification and verification of disabled persons (Divyangjan) for availing various government benefits globally.
authority: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
eligibility: Any Indian citizen having a benchmark disability as recognized under the RPwD Act 2016
documents: Recent color photograph
Signature or thumb impression
Address Proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID)
Identity Proof (Aadhaar, PAN)
Disability Certificate issued by a competent medical authority (if already available)

procedure: Visit the Swavlamban Card portal (swavlambancard.gov.in)
Click on 'Apply for Disability Certificate & UDID Card'
Fill in personal, disability, employment, and identity details
Upload scanned photograph, signature, and identity/address proofs
Submit to generate an enrolment number
Visit the designated district medical board for clinical assessment (if applying for a fresh certificate)
Post-approval, the e-UDID card can be downloaded, and the physical smart card is mailed

fees: Free of cost.
processingTime: 30 to 45 days after medical board assessment.

verification.notes: Verified against DEPwD UDID guidelines.

name: Udyam Registration Certificate
description: An electronic certificate issued to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in India to avail MSME-related schemes, subsidies, and priority sector lending.
authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
eligibility: Any person intending to establish a micro, small, or medium enterprise
Micro: Investment < ₹1 Cr, Turnover < ₹5 Cr
Small: Investment < ₹10 Cr, Turnover < ₹50 Cr
Medium: Investment < ₹50 Cr, Turnover < ₹250 Cr
documents: Aadhaar Number of the proprietor/managing partner/director
PAN Card of the business entity
Bank Account details (IFSC and Account Number)

procedure: Visit the official Udyam Registration portal (udyamregistration.gov.in)
Select 'For New Entrepreneurs who are not registered yet as MSME'
Validate Aadhaar using OTP
Validate PAN details (automatically fetches ITR and GST data if available)
Fill out enterprise details, bank information, NIC codes for manufacturing/services, and employment figures
Submit via final OTP and download the e-certificate immediately

fees: Free of cost. (No government fee is charged).
processingTime: Instant generation upon final OTP submission.

verification.notes: Verified against MSME Udyam registration guidelines.

name: Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID
description: A 14-digit unique health identifier that enables Indian citizens to securely access, manage, and share their digital health records with participating healthcare providers.
authority: National Health Authority (NHA)
eligibility: Any citizen of India
documents: Aadhaar Card (linked to mobile number for OTP) OR
Driving License / Mobile Number

procedure: Visit the ABHA portal (abha.abdm.gov.in) or use the ABHA mobile app
Click on 'Create ABHA Number'
Choose to create via Aadhaar (recommended for instant e-KYC) or Driving License
Enter the ID number, solve the captcha, and submit the OTP
Fill in basic profile details and create a custom ABHA address (similar to a UPI ID, e.g., name@abdm)
Download the digital ABHA card instantly

fees: Free of cost.
processingTime: Instant generation.

officialSources.sourceName: ABHA Portal - Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission

verification.notes: Verified against ABDM guidelines.

name: Income Certificate
description: An official state government document certifying the annual income of an individual or their family, essential for claiming scholarships, fee concessions, and welfare schemes.
authority: State Revenue Department (Tehsildar / SDM / Revenue Circle Officer)
eligibility: Any resident citizen of the respective state requiring proof of income
documents: Aadhaar Card
Address Proof (Ration Card, Voter ID, Electricity Bill)
Income Proof (Salary slip, IT Return, Form 16, or Affidavit)
Passport size photograph

procedure: Visit the respective State's e-District / e-Seva portal (e.g., edistrict.up.gov.in, sevasindhu.karnataka.gov.in)
Register as a citizen or visit the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) / Tehsildar office
Fill out the income certificate application form
Upload the required identity, address, and income proof documents (or an affidavit)
Pay the nominal processing fee
The application is verified by the local Patwari / Village Accountant, and the digital certificate is issued

fees: State-specific (Usually ranges from ₹15 to ₹50 as portal/CSC charges).
processingTime: 7 to 15 days.

officialSources.sourceName: National Portal of India - State e-District Links

verification.notes: Verified against generalized state revenue rules.

name: Caste Certificate (SC/ST)
description: A legal document serving as proof that a person belongs to a particular Scheduled Caste (SC) or Scheduled Tribe (ST), required for reservations in education and jobs.
authority: State Revenue Department (Tehsildar / SDM / District Magistrate)
eligibility: Must be an Indian citizen
Must belong to a caste/tribe explicitly listed in the Presidential Order for that specific state
documents: Identity Proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID)
Address Proof
Extract of birth register / school leaving certificate
Caste proof of father/blood relative (Old caste certificate or revenue record)
Affidavit (if required by state)

procedure: Apply via the respective State's e-District portal or at the local Tehsil/CSC
Fill the application detailing paternal ancestry and caste details
Upload the old caste certificate of a blood relative and identity proofs
Field verification is conducted by the revenue inspector/Patwari
Once approved, the digital caste certificate is generated

fees: State-specific (Usually ranges from ₹15 to ₹50 for CSC/portal fees).
processingTime: 15 to 30 days.

verification.notes: Verified against state e-district service catalogs.

name: OBC - Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) Certificate
description: A certificate issued to individuals belonging to Other Backward Classes who do not fall into the 'creamy layer' based on parental income/status, qualifying them for 27% reservation in central government jobs and education.
authority: State Revenue Department (Issued in Central Government Format by SDM/Tehsildar)
eligibility: Must belong to a caste listed in the Central List of OBCs for the respective state
Parental gross annual income must not exceed ₹8,00,000 for three consecutive years (excluding salary and agricultural income, subject to rule variations)
Parents must not hold Group A / Class I constitutional posts
documents: Identity and Address Proof
Caste proof of the applicant/father
Income proof of parents (ITR, Form 16, Salary Slip) for the last 3 years
Affidavit declaring non-creamy layer status

procedure: Obtain the Central Format for OBC-NCL certificate
Apply through the State's e-District portal or local SDM/Tehsildar office
Submit caste proofs and comprehensive income/wealth proofs of parents
After stringent revenue verification regarding income limits, the NCL certificate is issued (usually valid for 1 financial year for central exams)

fees: State-specific portal/CSC fees (nominal).
processingTime: 15 to 30 days.

officialSources.sourceName: National Commission for Backward Classes (Central List)

verification.notes: Verified against DoPT NCL guidelines.

name: Economically Weaker Section (EWS) Certificate
description: An income and asset certificate issued to citizens belonging to the General category (not covered under SC/ST/OBC) to avail 10% reservation in government jobs and educational institutions.
authority: State Revenue Department (District Magistrate / SDM / Tehsildar)
eligibility: Must NOT belong to SC, ST, or OBC categories
Gross annual family income must be below ₹8,00,000

Family must NOT own: 5 acres of agricultural land and above; Residential flat of 1000 sq ft and above; Residential plot of 100 sq yards and above in notified municipalities; or 200 sq yards and above elsewhere
documents: Aadhaar Card
Income proof (ITR, Salary Slips, Affidavit)
Property/Land documents (to prove asset limits are not breached)
Passport size photograph

procedure: Download the Annexure-I format for EWS Certificate (or apply via state e-District portal)
Submit the application with comprehensive family income and asset declarations
The Patwari/Revenue Inspector conducts a physical verification of land and property holdings
The Tehsildar/SDM issues the certificate (valid for one financial year)

fees: State-specific portal/CSC fees (nominal).
processingTime: 15 to 30 days.

verification.notes: Verified against DoPT EWS guidelines.

name: Domicile / Residence Certificate
description: An official document proving that a person is a permanent resident of a particular state/union territory, required for state-quota educational admissions and state government jobs.
authority: State Revenue Department (Tehsildar / SDM / District Collector)
eligibility: Must have resided in the state for a continuously prescribed number of years (varies by state, e.g., 7, 10, or 15 years)
Or must hold property in the state
Or must have been born in the state
documents: Aadhaar Card / Voter ID
Birth Certificate or School Leaving Certificate
Proof of continuous residence (Ration card, Electricity bills for the mandated period, Property tax receipts)
Affidavit of residence

procedure: Apply online on the State's e-District portal or at a CSC/Tehsil office
Upload identity proofs and long-term residence proofs spanning the required number of years
Police or Revenue Department verification may be conducted
The digital domicile certificate is issued post verification

fees: State-specific (Usually ₹15 to ₹50 portal charges).
processingTime: 10 to 20 days.

verification.notes: Verified against state e-district service requirements.

name: Birth Certificate
description: A vital record issued by local government authorities documenting the birth of a child, establishing age, identity, and citizenship rights (as per the RBD Act, 1969).
authority: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Corporation / Gram Panchayat)
eligibility: Any child born in India
Must be registered within 21 days of occurrence to be free of cost and straightforward
documents: Hospital discharge summary / birth proof from the medical institution
Parents' Aadhaar cards or valid IDs
Marriage certificate of parents (optional but helpful)
Affidavit/SDM order (if registration is delayed beyond 1 year)

procedure: For institutional births, the hospital reports the event to the local Registrar online
Parents can visit crsorgi.gov.in or the local municipal portal (e.g., e-Nagarpalika, NDMC) to download the certificate once generated
For non-institutional births or delayed registration, parents must apply manually at the local municipal office or Panchayat with an affidavit/SDM order

fees: Free if registered within 21 days. Nominal late fees apply for delays.
processingTime: 7 to 15 days for standard registration.

verification.notes: Verified against Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 guidelines.

name: Death Certificate
description: An official document issued by the government declaring the cause of death, location, and time, essential for property inheritance, insurance claims, and legal closures.
authority: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Corporation / Gram Panchayat)
eligibility: Next of kin or relatives of the deceased
Event must be registered within 21 days for standard processing
documents: Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (from the hospital/doctor)
Aadhaar card of the deceased (if available)
Aadhaar/ID of the applicant (informant)
Cremation/Burial ground receipt
Affidavit/SDM order (for delayed registration beyond 1 year)

procedure: If death occurs in a hospital, the institution reports it directly to the Registrar
For home deaths, the family must report to the local municipal/panchayat office with the cremation slip
Once registered, the death certificate can be downloaded from the CRS portal or local municipal web portal

fees: Free if registered within 21 days. Late fees apply thereafter.
processingTime: 7 to 15 days.

verification.notes: Verified against Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.

name: Marriage Registration Certificate
description: A legal certification of marriage between two individuals, required for passport applications, changing maiden names, joint bank accounts, and visa processing.
authority: Registrar of Marriages (State Revenue / Municipal Department)
eligibility: Groom must be at least 21 years old and Bride must be at least 18 years old
Marriage can be registered under the Hindu Marriage Act (HMA) or Special Marriage Act (SMA) depending on religion/preference
documents: Aadhaar Cards / Age proof of both parties
Wedding Invitation Card
Marriage Photographs (showing rituals/garland exchange)
Address proof of both parties
Affidavit of marriage
ID proof of 2 or 3 witnesses (varies by Act)

procedure: Apply online via the State's marriage registration portal (e.g., e-District, IGRS)
Upload the required documents and photos
Book an appointment with the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) or Marriage Registrar
Both parties along with the witnesses must appear physically before the Registrar
Sign the registry, after which the digital/physical certificate is issued

fees: State-specific (Typically ₹100 under HMA, ₹150 under SMA, plus processing fees).
processingTime: Same day of appointment to 15 days.

verification.notes: Verified against standard state marriage registration rules.

name: Legal Heir / Surviving Member Certificate
description: A certificate establishing the relationship of the heirs to a deceased person, used for transferring utility connections, claiming provident fund, and insurance benefits.
authority: State Revenue Department (Tehsildar / SDM) or Civil Court
eligibility: Immediate family members (Spouse, Children, Parents) of the deceased person
documents: Original Death Certificate of the deceased
Identity and Address proof of all surviving members
Affidavit declaring all legal heirs
Ration Card or Family Tree document

procedure: Apply via the State's e-District portal or at the local Tehsildar's office
Submit the application with death certificate and IDs of all heirs
The Revenue Inspector and Village Administrative Officer conduct a local inquiry to confirm the surviving members
Upon satisfactory report, the Tehsildar issues the Legal Heir Certificate

fees: State-specific (Usually nominal portal fees).
processingTime: 15 to 30 days.

verification.notes: Verified against state revenue department manuals.

name: Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
description: A crucial document issued by the registration authority confirming that a property is free from monetary and legal liabilities (like mortgages or uncleared loans).
authority: Inspector General of Registration and Stamps (IGRS) of the State
eligibility: Property owners, prospective buyers, or banks assessing loan eligibility
documents: Property Details (Survey Number, Khata Number, Document Number)
Address Proof of Applicant
Copy of previous Sale Deed / Title Deed

procedure: Visit the State's IGRS portal (e.g., Kaveri Online for Karnataka, IGRS AP/UP)
Select the option to 'Search/Apply for Encumbrance Certificate'
Enter property details, SRO (Sub-Registrar Office) name, and the required search period (e.g., 15 or 30 years)
Pay the search fee online
The digitally signed EC (Form 15 if encumbrances exist, Form 16 if nil) can be downloaded, or physical copies can be collected from the SRO

fees: State-specific (Varies based on the number of years searched).
processingTime: Instant (if digitized online) to 7 days (manual search).

verification.notes: Verified against state IGRS guidelines.

name: Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) - Passport
description: A certificate issued by the Passport Office or Police authorities verifying that the applicant has no criminal record, mandatory for employment, long-term visas, or emigration abroad.
authority: Ministry of External Affairs (Passport Seva) / Local State Police
eligibility: Indian citizens holding a valid passport seeking employment, residential status, or long-term visa abroad
Tourists travelling on short-term visas do not usually require a PCC
documents: Valid Indian Passport
Present Address Proof
Employment Contract / Visa Letter from the foreign embassy or employer

procedure: Log in to the Passport Seva portal and click on 'Apply for Police Clearance Certificate'
Fill the online form specifying the country for which PCC is required and the purpose
Pay the fee and book an appointment at the PSK/POPSK
Visit the PSK with the original passport and visa/offer letter
Post-PSK visit, a police verification is initiated; upon clear report, the PCC is printed and dispatched/handed over

processingTime: 7 to 21 days (depending on the speed of local police verification).

verification.notes: Verified against MEA Passport Seva guidelines.

name: International Driving Permit (IDP)
description: A translation of your Indian driving license allowing you to drive motor vehicles in foreign countries that are signatories to the 1949 Geneva Convention.
authority: State RTOs / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
eligibility: Must hold a valid Indian Driving License
Must hold a valid Indian Passport and Visa for the destination country
The IDP is valid for 1 year or until the driving license expires, whichever is earlier
documents: Valid Driving License
Valid Passport and Visa
Air ticket / Boarding Pass (sometimes required)
Form 4A application and Medical Certificate Form 1A
Passport size photographs

procedure: Go to the Sarathi Parivahan portal and select 'Apply for International Driving Permit (IDP)'
Enter DL Number and Date of Birth
Upload required passport, visa, and medical documents
Pay the IDP fee online
Visit the respective RTO for document verification
The IDP is usually issued on the same day over the counter after verification

processingTime: 1 to 3 days (often same-day issue at RTO).

verification.notes: Verified against MoRTH Parivahan guidelines.

name: Ration Card (NFSA)
description: An official document issued by state governments to eligible households to purchase subsidized food grains under the National Food Security Act (NFSA).
authority: Department of Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs (State Governments)
eligibility: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY): Poorest of the poor families
Priority Household (PHH): Families meeting state-specific vulnerability and income criteria
Applicant must be an Indian citizen and not possess a ration card in another state
documents: Aadhaar Cards of all family members
Income Certificate
Address Proof (Electricity Bill, Water Bill)
Passport size photograph of the Head of the Family (usually the eldest female)

procedure: Apply via the State Food and Civil Supplies portal or the National Food Security portal via 'Common Registration Facility'
Fill the application detailing family composition and upload Aadhaar/Income proofs
Submit the form online or at a local CSC / Tehsil office
Field verification is conducted by the Food Inspector to check economic status
Upon approval, the physical/smart Ration Card is issued

fees: State-specific (Usually ranges from ₹5 to ₹45).
processingTime: 15 to 45 days.

verification.notes: Verified against NFSA common registration facility guidelines.

name: FSSAI Basic Registration Certificate
description: A mandatory food safety registration for petty food business operators (FBOs) manufacturing or selling food products, ensuring compliance with hygiene standards.
authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
eligibility: Petty Food Business Operators with an annual turnover not exceeding ₹12 Lakhs
Includes hawkers, street vendors, small retailers, and home-based food makers
(Larger businesses require a State or Central License instead of Basic Registration)
documents: Photo Identity Proof (Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID)
Passport size photograph of the applicant
Proof of Address of the business premises
Declaration form

procedure: Visit the FoSCoS (Food Safety Compliance System) portal
Select 'Apply for License/Registration' and specify the state and turnover (< ₹12 Lakhs)
Fill out Form A (for Basic Registration)
Upload the required documents and photo
Pay the registration fee online
The registration certificate with a 14-digit FSSAI number is generated and can be downloaded

fees: ₹100 per year (can be applied for up to 5 years at a time).
processingTime: 7 to 30 days (often generated faster if no inspection is flagged).

verification.notes: Verified against FSSAI FoSCoS guidelines.

name: Import Export Code (IEC)
description: A key business identification number mandatory for exports or imports from/to India, issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
authority: Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry
eligibility: Any individual, proprietorship, partnership, LLP, or company intending to import or export goods/services in India
documents: PAN Card of the individual/business entity
Applicant's Aadhaar Card
Cancelled Cheque bearing the entity's pre-printed name or Bank Certificate
Address Proof of the business

procedure: Visit the official DGFT portal
Register and create a profile
Click on 'Apply for IEC'
Fill out the entity details, directors/partners info, and bank details
Upload the cancelled cheque and sign the application digitally using Aadhaar e-Sign or DSC
Pay the application fee
The IEC certificate (e-IEC) is auto-generated and dispatched via email

processingTime: Instant to 1 working day (auto-generated in most cases).

verification.notes: Verified against DGFT online IEC issuance process.

name: GST Registration Certificate
description: A certificate issued to businesses registering under the Goods and Services Tax framework, bearing a 15-digit Goods and Services Tax Identification Number (GSTIN).
authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) / State Commercial Tax Departments
eligibility: Businesses involved in the supply of goods with a turnover exceeding ₹40 Lakhs (₹20 Lakhs in Special Category States)
Businesses involved in the supply of services with a turnover exceeding ₹20 Lakhs (₹10 Lakhs in Special Category States)
Entities involved in inter-state supply, e-commerce operators, or paying tax under the reverse charge mechanism (mandatory regardless of turnover)
documents: PAN Card of the Business / Applicant
Aadhaar Card of Promoters/Directors
Proof of Business Registration (Incorporation Certificate, Partnership Deed)
Address Proof of the Principal Place of Business (Rent agreement, Electricity bill)
Bank Account details (Cancelled cheque/statement)

procedure: Visit the GST Portal and select 'New Registration'
Fill Part A to generate a Temporary Reference Number (TRN) using PAN, Mobile, and Email
Log in with TRN and fill Part B detailing business, promoters, authorized signatories, and places of business
Upload required documents and authenticate using Aadhaar e-Sign or DSC
Submit the application (Form GST REG-01)
Post tax officer verification, the Registration Certificate (Form GST REG-06) is issued

fees: Free of cost (No government fee for registration).
processingTime: 3 to 7 working days (subject to Aadhaar authentication and officer queries).

verification.notes: Verified against GST portal registration rules.

name: Vehicle Registration Certificate (RC)
description: An official document proving that your motor vehicle is registered with the Indian Government, validating the legal ownership of the vehicle.
authority: State RTOs / Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH)
eligibility: Any person or entity purchasing a motor vehicle in India
documents: Application Form 20
Sales Certificate (Form 21) issued by the dealer
Road Worthiness Certificate (Form 22) from the manufacturer
Valid Vehicle Insurance
Address Proof and Identity Proof of the owner
Customs Clearance Certificate (for imported vehicles)

procedure: Usually, the automobile dealer applies on behalf of the buyer through the Vahan portal at the time of purchase
The dealer uploads the forms, pays the road tax and registration fees online
The vehicle is inspected by the RTO (or dealer via automated systems)
The RTO assigns a registration number and dispatches the Smart Card RC via post to the owner's address

fees: Varies by state (Includes Registration Fee ₹600 for cars/₹300 for bikes, plus Smart Card fee ₹200, plus State Road Tax based on vehicle cost).
processingTime: 7 to 30 days.

verification.notes: Verified against MoRTH Vahan guidelines.

name: APAAR ID (Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry)
description: A 'One Nation, One Student ID' providing a lifelong 12-digit unique identifier to students in India to digitally store and track academic credits, degrees, and extracurricular achievements.
authority: Ministry of Education / Academic Bank of Credits (ABC)
eligibility: All students enrolled in schools, colleges, and higher educational institutions in India
documents: Aadhaar Card (linked to a mobile number for OTP)
DigiLocker Account

procedure: Schools/Colleges usually initiate the process by obtaining consent from parents/students
Students can also self-register via the APAAR portal (apaar.education.gov.in) or the Academic Bank of Credits (ABC) portal
Login using DigiLocker credentials
Provide Aadhaar consent for e-KYC
The system generates the 12-digit APAAR ID instantly, which can be downloaded as a digital card

fees: Free of cost.
processingTime: Instant generation.

verification.notes: Verified against Ministry of Education APAAR launch guidelines.

name: Shop and Establishment Certificate (Gumasta License)
description: A state-level registration mandatory for commercial establishments, shops, and businesses operating within municipal limits, regulating working hours, wages, and employee rights.
authority: State Labour Department
eligibility: Any shop, commercial establishment, hotel, restaurant, or place of public amusement/entertainment
Required even for sole proprietors operating from a commercial space
documents: Identity Proof of Employer (Aadhaar, PAN)
Address Proof of the Establishment (Rent Agreement, Property Tax Receipt, Electricity Bill)
Photograph of the establishment with the signboard
Details of employees

procedure: Visit the respective State's Labour Department portal (e.g., lms.mahaonline.gov.in for Maharashtra, labour.delhi.gov.in)
Create an employer login profile
Fill in Form A (or equivalent state form) specifying business activity, employee count, and working hours
Upload documents and pay the prescribed fee
The Labour Inspector verifies the application, and the digital certificate is issued (often generated instantly for small shops in reformed states)

fees: State-specific (Varies based on the number of employees, e.g., Free for 0-9 employees in Maharashtra, fees apply for more).
processingTime: Instant to 15 days.

verification.notes: Verified against state labour department regulations.

name: Trade License
description: A certificate/license issued by the local municipality permitting a business to carry on a particular trade or business in a specific location, ensuring compliance with local zoning and safety rules.
authority: Local Municipal Corporation / Urban Local Body (ULB)
eligibility: Any individual or entity wishing to start a commercial business within a municipal limit
The business must not be offensive, dangerous, or a nuisance to the public
documents: ID Proof of the Applicant (Aadhaar, PAN)
Property Tax Receipt / Lease Agreement of the business premises
NOC from the immediate neighbor / landlord
Layout plan of the premises
Fire NOC (if applicable for hazardous trades)

procedure: Visit the online portal of the respective Municipal Corporation (e.g., mcdonline.nic.in, bbmp.gov.in)
Select the 'Trade License' application section
Fill in the nature of the trade, premises details, and upload documents
The Health Inspector or Ward Officer assesses the application and computes the fee
Pay the trade license fee online to generate the certificate

fees: Municipality-specific (Varies based on trade type, area, and turnover).
processingTime: 15 to 30 days.

officialSources.sourceName: National Portal of India - Municipal Services

verification.notes: Verified against municipal corporation business regulations.

name: Central Arms License
description: A legal permit issued by the government under the Arms Act, 1959, authorizing an individual to own, possess, or carry a firearm for self-defense, crop protection, or sports.
authority: Ministry of Home Affairs (NDAL-ALIS) / State Licensing Authorities (DM / Commissioner of Police)
eligibility: Must be an Indian citizen of sound mind
Minimum 21 years of age
Must have a genuine reason (e.g., threat to life, sports shooting, crop protection)
Must not have a criminal record or be prohibited under the Arms Act
documents: Identity Proof (Aadhaar, Voter ID, Passport)
Address Proof
Medical Fitness Certificate (Mental & Physical)
Proof of Age
Safe storage declaration
Supporting documents for the threat/need (e.g., FIRs, sports certificates)

procedure: Submit the application online via the National Database of Arms Licenses (NDAL-ALIS) portal
Upload required documents and pay the application fee
The application is forwarded to the local police station for intense background and antecedent verification
An interview is conducted by the Licensing Authority (DM / DCP)
If approved, the applicant is granted the license and can purchase the firearm, which is then registered on the license booklet

fees: Varies by weapon type (e.g., ₹1000 application fee + additional grant fees as per Arms Rules 2016).
processingTime: 60 to 90 days (often longer depending on police verification speed).

officialSources.sourceName: NDAL-ALIS Portal - Ministry of Home Affairs

verification.notes: Verified against Arms Rules 2016 and NDAL-ALIS guidelines.
